definitionEn: full of energy, initiative and new ideas for practical or business projects
situation: Someone comes up with practical, sometimes risky ideas and takes the initiative to turn them into real projects or businesses.

examples.text: An [[enterprising]] student turned his hobby of repairing bikes into a small business.
The charity relies on [[enterprising]] volunteers who keep finding new ways to raise money.
Local shopkeepers came up with [[enterprising]] solutions to survive the shortage of supplies.

texts: She's always been [[enterprising]], even as a child selling lemonade on the corner.
The council is looking for [[enterprising]] local businesses to fill the empty shops.
His most [[enterprising]] idea yet is a bakery that delivers by bicycle.

badCollocation.text: The country built an [[enterprising]] network of highways connecting every region.
badCollocation.noteRu: Enterprising описывает людей или компании, проявляющие инициативу, а не масштаб инфраструктуры. Про дороги сказали бы extensive/impressive network.

collocationTask.prompt: The award goes to the most ___ young entrepreneur of the year.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Нужно прилагательное enterprising перед entrepreneur. Enterprise — существительное, spacious и obedient не подходят по смыслу.

nuance.text: The [[enterprising]] shop owner turned her empty storeroom into a popular café.
nuance.explanationRu: Enterprising — про практическую находчивость и инициативу в конкретном деле. Ambitious — про стремление к успеху вообще, необязательно связанное с конкретной идеей.

reverse.text: He was always [[ambitious]], dreaming of running his own company one day.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о мечте — ambitious. Enterprising потребовало бы конкретных практических действий, а не просто желания.

fixIt.text: The [[ambitious]] shopkeeper turned unsold bread into a thriving side business selling breadcrumbs to local restaurants.
fixIt.explanationRu: Про находчивую, практичную идею говорят enterprising. Ambitious — про амбиции вообще, здесь важнее именно находчивость.

wordFormation.text: Turning a hobby into a small business takes real [[enterprising]] spirit and a bit of luck.

reply.context: A colleague says: "Did you hear Sam turned his old garage into a small repair shop that's actually making money?"
options: That's so enterprising of him — he's always finding new opportunities.
Wow, his garage sounds really enterprising, it must be huge.
One must applaud such an enterprising commercial undertaking on his part.
reply.explanationRu: Первый вариант хвалит именно человека — это верно. Во втором enterprising ошибочно описывает гараж. Третий звучит слишком официально для разговора с коллегой.

definitionEn: a person who is extremely interested in and excited about a particular activity or subject
situation: You talk about someone who is deeply and genuinely passionate about a particular hobby, sport or subject, often knowing a great deal about it.

examples.text: The vintage car rally attracted [[enthusiasts]] from all over the country.
As a lifelong wine [[enthusiast]], she can name a grape variety from a single sip.
The forum is full of amateur astronomy [[enthusiasts]] who share photos of the night sky.

texts: He's a real football [[enthusiast]] who never misses a match, home or away.
The museum runs workshops for young science [[enthusiasts]] every weekend.
Local history [[enthusiasts]] helped restore the old railway station by hand.

badCollocation.text: She's very [[enthusiast]] about starting her new job next week.
badCollocation.noteRu: После very нужно прилагательное — enthusiastic. Enthusiast — существительное («человек-энтузиаст»), не прилагательное.

collocationTask.prompt: The club welcomes new ___ of all ages and skill levels.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Клуб принимает enthusiasts — увлечённых людей любого уровня. Experts подразумевает высокий уровень (противоречит «всех уровней»), officials и sceptics по смыслу не подходят.

nuance.text: He's a genuine railway [[enthusiast]], even though he's never actually driven a train.
nuance.explanationRu: Enthusiast — человек, увлечённый темой, необязательно профессионал. Expert подразумевает высокий уровень знаний или навыков, а не просто увлечённость.

reverse.text: You should ask Maria, she's a genuine legal [[expert]] with twenty years of experience.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь важен профессиональный уровень — expert. Enthusiast говорил бы только об увлечённости темой, а не о реальном опыте и квалификации.

fixIt.text: He calls himself a wine [[expert]], but really he just enjoys trying a new bottle every weekend.
fixIt.explanationRu: Раз человек просто любит пробовать вино для удовольствия, а не является профессионалом, нужно enthusiast, а не expert.

wordFormation.text: Even after losing the first match, the team stayed remarkably [[enthusiastic]] about their chances.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Why does Leo know so much about vintage cameras?"
options: He's a real enthusiast — he's been collecting them for years.
He's a real enthusiast, it's parked right outside actually.
He is to be regarded as a connoisseur of considerable enthusiast standing.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ верно называет его увлечённым человеком. Во втором enthusiast перепутан с самим предметом. Третий звучит неестественно официально для разговора с другом.

rewrite.original: My uncle loves everything about trains and has done since he was a boy.
rewrite.frame: My uncle is a real train ____ and has been since he was a boy.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Loves everything about trains» одним словом — enthusiast.

definitionEn: to give someone an official or legal right to have or do something
senseNote: Выбрано значение «давать право» (entitle someone to something), а не «давать название» книге или статье — более простое и распространённое употребление.
situation: A rule, ticket, membership or law officially gives someone the right to receive or do a particular thing.

examples.text: Owning a season ticket [[entitles]] you to priority booking for cup matches.
Staff who work night shifts are [[entitled]] to an extra day of holiday each year.
The scholarship [[entitles]] recipients to free accommodation for the whole degree.

texts: Every full-time employee is [[entitled]] to at least twenty days of paid leave.
Passengers with a valid rail card are [[entitled]] to a third off standard fares.
As a shareholder, she was [[entitled]] to vote at the annual meeting.

badCollocation.text: This voucher will [[entitle]] to a free coffee with any sandwich.
badCollocation.noteRu: Entitle требует, кого именно наделяют правом: entitle YOU/THE HOLDER to a free coffee. Без объекта-человека предложение неполное.

collocationTask.prompt: Being a gold member ___ you to free upgrades on every flight.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Entitle you TO something — фиксированная конструкция («даёт право на»). Allow, permit, let так с to + существительным не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Two years of continuous service [[entitles]] employees to a full month of paid leave.
nuance.explanationRu: Entitle требует to: entitled TO something. Qualify обычно требует for: qualifies FOR something — с to здесь будет грамматическая ошибка.

reverse.text: Only candidates with a nursing degree [[qualify]] for this particular position.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь нужен qualify FOR — «соответствовать критериям». Entitle потребовало бы другого предлога (to) и оттенка «право», а не «соответствие».

fixIt.text: Two years of continuous service [[qualifies]] employees to a full month of paid leave every year.
fixIt.explanationRu: После to (entitled TO something) нужен entitle. Qualify обычно идёт с for, а не с to — с to это ошибка.

wordFormation.text: Knowing your legal [[entitlement]] to sick pay can save you a lot of stress later.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Do part-time staff get any paid holiday here?"
options: Yes, everyone's entitled to holiday pay based on the hours they work.
Yes, the building is entitled Riverside House, I think.
Indeed, all part-time personnel are hereby entitled to statutory leave entitlements.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ верно использует entitled («иметь право»). Во втором entitle перепутан со значением «дать название». Третий звучит как официальный документ.

rewrite.original: Because she has a student card, she can get half-price tickets at the cinema.
rewrite.frame: Her student card ____ her to half-price tickets at the cinema.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Can get... because of the card» = the card entitles her to...

definitionEn: something that exists as a single, separate and independent thing
situation: You want to describe something, often an organisation, company or concept, as existing on its own with a clear, separate identity.

examples.text: Although the two brands share an office, they remain legally separate [[entities]].
Philosophers have long debated whether the mind is a distinct [[entity]] from the brain.
The new department will operate as an independent [[entity]] within the university.

texts: For tax purposes, the charity is treated as a separate [[entity]] from its founder.
Some scientists argue that consciousness cannot be reduced to a single physical [[entity]].
The new agency will function as an independent [[entity]], answerable only to parliament.

badCollocation.text: A mysterious [[entity]] knocked on my door last night asking for directions.
badCollocation.noteRu: Про обычного человека так не говорят — entity звучит слишком абстрактно и безлично. Нужно person или just someone; entity — для организаций и абстрактных объектов.

collocationTask.prompt: The two companies merged but still operate as separate legal ___.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Про организации, существующие отдельно, говорят legal entities. Objects, materials, documents сюда не подходят по смыслу.

nuance.text: Each subsidiary is registered as a separate legal [[entity]] in its own country.
nuance.explanationRu: Entity подчёркивает отдельное юридическое существование как таковое. Organisation говорит скорее о структуре и людях внутри неё — это чуть другой акцент.

reverse.text: The charity is a well-known [[organisation]] that helps homeless people find shelter.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь важна структура и люди, помогающие бездомным — organisation. Entity звучало бы слишком абстрактно и обезличенно для этого контекста.

fixIt.text: Although they share a logo, the two divisions are legally separate [[products]] with completely different owners.
fixIt.explanationRu: Про подразделения, существующие как отдельные юридические лица, говорят entities. Products — это «продукты», подразделения ими не являются.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "Wait, isn't this new spin-off part of the parent company?"
options: Actually no, it's been set up as a completely separate legal entity.
Actually no, it's basically an alien entity that landed here yesterday.
Negative, the aforementioned entity operates autonomously pursuant to its own charter.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ верно объясняет юридическую самостоятельность. Во втором entity употреблён в фантастическом смысле («существо»). Третий звучит как юридический документ.

rewrite.original: Even though they work closely together, the two organisations are legally independent of each other.
rewrite.frame: Even though they work closely together, the two organisations are legally separate ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Legally independent of each other» = legally separate entities.

definitionEn: an extremely fast, widespread increase in something harmful across a population
senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение — стремительное, неконтролируемое распространение чего-то нежелательного, необязательно болезни: epidemic of loneliness/violence/obesity; буквальное значение «эпидемия болезни» отдельно не тренируется.
situation: Something harmful, such as loneliness, violence or a bad habit, spreads extremely quickly and widely through a whole society.

examples.text: Public health officials have described rising knife crime among teenagers as an [[epidemic]].
Some researchers now talk about an [[epidemic]] of loneliness among people who live alone in big cities.
Fast food and sugary drinks have been blamed for the childhood obesity [[epidemic]] in many rich countries.

texts: Commentators are calling loneliness among the elderly a silent [[epidemic]].
The country is facing what doctors call an [[epidemic]] of stress-related illness.
Some call binge-watching an [[epidemic]] of modern entertainment habits.

badCollocation.text: The town suffered an [[epidemic]] when a single house burned down last month.
badCollocation.noteRu: Epidemic — это массовое, широко распространённое явление, а не единичный случай. Один сгоревший дом — это incident/case, а не epidemic.

collocationTask.prompt: Doctors are warning of a growing ___ of anxiety among teenagers.
collocationTask.explanationRu: О массовом, стремительно растущем явлении говорят epidemic. Incident — единичный случай, exception — исключение, symptom — лишь один из признаков.

nuance.text: What began as a local problem has grown into a full [[epidemic]] of shoplifting across the region.
nuance.explanationRu: Epidemic — уже широко распространившееся, масштабное явление. Outbreak — скорее «вспышка», начало и часто локальное явление; здесь важен именно масштаб.

reverse.text: Doctors reported a small [[outbreak]] of food poisoning linked to a single restaurant.
reverse.explanationRu: Один ресторан и небольшая вспышка — это outbreak. Epidemic подразумевало бы гораздо более широкое распространение.

fixIt.text: What began as a local problem has grown into a full [[outbreak]] of shoplifting across the entire region.
fixIt.explanationRu: Раз явление уже распространилось по всему региону, а не только начинается, нужно epidemic, а не outbreak — обычно локальная вспышка.

reply.context: A friend says: "Everyone at work seems completely burnt out these days."
options: I know, honestly it feels like an epidemic of exhaustion right now.
I know, I think there's literally a virus epidemic in the office fridge.
Indeed, one might characterise the prevailing condition as an occupational epidemic of considerable magnitude.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ уместен и использует epidemic в переносном смысле. Второй сводит его к буквальному вирусу, не в тему. Третий звучит слишком по-научному для беседы с другом.

rewrite.original: It feels as if almost everyone you meet these days complains of feeling constantly tired.
rewrite.frame: It feels as if there's a real ____ of exhaustion these days.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Almost everyone complains of the same problem» одним словом можно описать как epidemic.

definitionEn: the state of having the same rights, status and opportunities as everyone else
senseNote: Выбрано социально-правовое значение «равноправие, равенство прав и возможностей», а не более простое «равенство в количестве или размере» (например, в математике).
situation: People are treated fairly and given the same rights, status and opportunities in society, regardless of gender, race or background.

examples.text: The new law was a major step towards gender [[equality]] in the workplace.
Campaigners have fought for decades to achieve racial [[equality]] before the law.
True [[equality]] means equal pay for equal work, regardless of gender.

texts: The charter promises [[equality]] for all citizens, whatever their background.
Progress on gender [[equality]] has been painfully slow in some industries.
The movement's main goal has always been racial [[equality]].

badCollocation.text: After careful measuring, we confirmed the [[equality]] of the two boxes in size.
badCollocation.noteRu: Про одинаковый размер предметов говорят that they are equal / the same size, а не equality — это слово почти всегда о правах и равенстве между людьми.

collocationTask.prompt: The charity campaigns for greater ___ between men and women at work.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Про равные права мужчин и женщин говорят equality. Equation — это «уравнение» (математика), similarity и balance по смыслу не подходят.

nuance.text: The report calls for greater [[equality]] between rich and poor regions of the country.
nuance.explanationRu: Equality — «равенство» (в правах, статусе). Equation — совершенно другое слово, «уравнение» (математика); их часто путают из-за похожего написания.

reverse.text: Solving the [[equation]] took the students almost the entire lesson.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь о математическом уравнении — equation. Equality («равенство прав») сюда совершенно не подходит по смыслу.

fixIt.text: The report calls for greater [[equation]] between rich and poor regions of the country.
fixIt.explanationRu: Нужно equality — «равенство» (в правах, возможностях). Equation — это «уравнение», к правам регионов не относится.

wordFormation.text: The reforms aim to guarantee full [[equality]] between all social classes within a generation.

reply.context: A friend asks: "What's the charity you volunteer for actually campaigning for?"
options: Mainly gender equality — equal pay, equal opportunities, that kind of thing.
Mainly gender equality, like making sure both team scores end up the same.
The organisation in question advocates for the attainment of comprehensive socio-economic equality.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ верно объясняет социальное равенство. Во втором equality сведено к «одинаковому счёту в игре» — не тот смысл. Третий звучит как академический доклад.

rewrite.original: The new policy tries to make sure men and women get exactly the same pay for the same work.
rewrite.frame: The new policy tries to promote pay ____ between men and women.
rewrite.explanationRu: «Exactly the same pay for the same work» = pay equality.

definitionEn: a situation or problem that involves several factors which must all be taken into account
senseNote: Выбрано переносное значение — «совокупность факторов, которые нужно учитывать при решении» (part of the equation, bring into the equation), а не буквальное математическое уравнение.
situation: You want to say that a particular factor is, or should be, one of several things considered together when making a decision.

examples.text: Rising rents are just one part of the [[equation]] when people decide whether to move abroad.
Once you bring childcare costs into the [[equation]], going back to work part-time barely pays.
Climate change now has to be part of any serious [[equation]] about future farming policy.

texts: Job security is a big part of the [[equation]] for most people choosing a career.
Once you add commuting time into the [[equation]], the cheaper flat isn't such a bargain.
For many couples, in-laws are an unexpected part of the marriage [[equation]].

badCollocation.text: We need to solve the [[equation]] of whether to move house or stay put.
badCollocation.noteRu: Переносное equation не «решают» (solve) — так говорят только про математические уравнения. Про совокупность факторов говорят part of/bring into the equation.

collocationTask.prompt: Cost is definitely part of the ___ when choosing a university.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивая фраза part of the equation — «один из факторов». Agreement, ceremony, habit по смыслу не подходят.

nuance.text: Once you factor in the maintenance costs, the cheap car doesn't look so cheap in the overall [[equation]].
nuance.explanationRu: Equation в этом значении — «общая картина», совокупность факторов при принятии решения. Calculation — более буквально «подсчёт», акцент на цифрах, а не на факторах вообще.

reverse.text: The final [[calculation]] showed we'd spent almost twice our original budget on repairs.
reverse.explanationRu: Здесь речь именно о подсчёте суммы — calculation. Equation в переносном смысле говорило бы о факторах решения, а не о числовом итоге.

fixIt.text: Once you factor in the maintenance costs, the cheap car doesn't look so cheap in the overall [[calculation]].
fixIt.explanationRu: Про совокупность факторов при выборе говорят part of/in the equation. Calculation здесь слишком буквально про цифры, а не про общую картину.

wordFormation.text: Rising rents and stagnant wages have created a difficult [[equation]] for many young families.

reply.context: A colleague says: "Honestly, I don't know if I should take the higher-paying job in another city."
options: Don't forget to bring your partner's career into the equation too.
Don't forget, two plus two is definitely part of the equation here.
One must, of course, incorporate all pertinent variables into the overarching equation.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ верно использует equation в переносном смысле. Во втором это буквальная математика не в тему. Третий звучит слишком по-канцелярски для совета коллеге.

rewrite.original: When deciding where to live, you also have to think about how close it is to your parents.
rewrite.frame: When deciding where to live, proximity to your parents is also part of the ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: «One of the things you have to think about» = part of the equation.

definitionEn: to build or put up a structure, especially in a formal or official way
senseNote: Выбрано значение «возводить, строить» (памятник, здание, конструкцию), не анатомическое значение слова erect как прилагательного.
situation: Workers or an organisation formally put up a large structure, such as a building, statue, tent or piece of scaffolding.

examples.text: Volunteers worked through the night to [[erect]] the festival's main stage before the rain arrived.
The town council voted to [[erect]] a statue in honour of the nurses who worked through the crisis.
Engineers took only three days to [[erect]] the temporary bridge across the flooded river.

texts: It took a whole team to [[erect]] the marquee before the wedding guests arrived.
Soldiers were sent to [[erect]] barriers along the flooded riverbank.
The company plans to [[erect]] a new warehouse on the edge of town.

badCollocation.text: She [[erected]] her hand to ask the lecturer a question.
badCollocation.noteRu: Руку не erect, а raise — «поднять». Erect — «возводить» крупные конструкции: здания, статуи, палатки, леса.

collocationTask.prompt: It took the whole team a week to ___ the new scaffolding.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Строительные леса, здания, палатки erect — «возводят». Fold, paint, grow по смыслу не подходят к возведению конструкции.

nuance.text: The team needed heavy machinery to [[erect]] the enormous steel frame of the new stadium.
nuance.explanationRu: Erect — целенаправленно возвести крупную конструкцию (здание, статую, леса). Raise — более общее «поднять» (руку, флаг, вопрос, деньги), не про строительство.

reverse.text: Thousands of people [[raised]] their hands to vote against the new proposal.
reverse.explanationRu: Поднять руку — raise, а не erect. Erect используется только для возведения крупных конструкций, не для частей тела.

fixIt.text: Workers [[planted]] a massive steel-frame stage for the festival in less than a week.
fixIt.explanationRu: Крупную конструкцию (сцену, здание, леса) erect — «возводят». Plant — «сажать» растения или «водружать» флаг, не подходит для конструкции такого масштаба.

wordFormation.text: The [[erection]] of temporary flood barriers along the riverbank took engineers less than two days.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How long do you think it'll take to get the festival stage ready?"
options: The crew usually manage to erect the whole thing in about a day.
The crew usually manage to erect their lunch break by midday.
The workforce shall endeavour to erect the aforementioned structure with due expedience.
reply.explanationRu: Первый ответ естественно описывает возведение сцены. Во втором erect использован бессмысленно. Третий звучит слишком официально для разговора с коллегой.

rewrite.original: Local volunteers put up a temporary shelter for flood victims within just two days.
rewrite.frame: Local volunteers ____ a temporary shelter for flood victims within just two days.
